text:
R322 — persistent serve prefill retirement and same-base expert-cache growth
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Scope: read-only source audit of candidate W e3c904e2, corrected to the owner-specified actual `--serve` controller route: persistent engine, GEN requests, 8,192 prefill chunk, 144-slot/281-MiB per-layer expert cache, no MTP, no prefill borrowing, CPU prefill share/gate off, prefill-first off, max context 262,144, int8 KV resident 32,768, no KVGrow. No source changes, model/GPU/process work, build/test/import/profiler, Git mutation, cleanup or active Main receipt inspection. The owner confirms the qualified controller argv includes `--serve`; the exact supplied task does not confirm `--vram-elastic`, so I do not assume that flag or VMM support is active.

Correction to R321
R321's claimed seam at `generate.cpp:10300–10683` is in the standalone one-shot generation path, below the persistent serve branch's early return. It is inapplicable to the measured `--serve` controller. The original R321 artifact remains unchanged. This report follows the persistent setup at 5753–6040 and request loop at 7807–10220.

Decision
Retiring the owned Prefill workspace can create physical headroom during decode in the persistent engine, but there is no safe immediate source-only knob to spend that headroom on more expert slots. `Prefill sp` is created, initialized with its own buffers and kept alive for the server lifetime; the `Verifier` and its graph-capable cache bindings are initialized before any request. Every later fresh GEN prompt reuses `sp`. A useful design must therefore support a serialized two-way transition: retire Prefill after each successful prompt before decode/cache expansion, then shrink the extra cache slots and reinitialize Prefill before the next prompt.

The same-base VMM idea is possible only after a focused cache-layout and owner-capacity refactor. Current `ExpertCache::open_segmented` reserves exactly the requested cache bytes and maps every segment at open; `grow()` can only map a previously unmapped tail within that fixed reservation. The current 144-slot cache has no reserved tail. The explicit `--vram-elastic` path is not sufficient by itself, and its selection is not established by the argv information supplied for this audit.

Persistent route lifecycle
- Startup creates persistent `Prefill sp` at generate.cpp:5769. With `--no-prefill-borrow`, the `borrow` pointer remains null; `sp.init` allocates its chunk buffers separately before READY (5777–5837). The same `sp` instance is used by the request loop's `read_part` lambda (8922–8929). It must be initialized again after any reset before a future `sp.run`.
- The main `Verifier ver` is initialized before READY at 6012–6019. `VerifyHits` binds the cache base, slot offsets, and `n_slots` at 5852–5859. When device-plan/resident-graph support is enabled, `Verifier::init` copies exactly `hits.n_slots` slot offsets into its own device allocation (verify.cpp:435–441); graph capture then retains the cache base and that copied offset table. A cache grow after startup cannot make new slots visible by merely updating `xcache.slots()` or `d_res`.
- A successful prompt traverses request segmentation and `sp.run`, then final borrowed-slot refill and residency upload, `cpu_jobs.finish`, and `prompt done` (generate.cpp:9093–9181). In the no-borrow route, the `lent_now` refill is empty, but Prefill's private copy stream can have remaining work. `Prefill::reset()` is the available reusable teardown; it drains compute and copy queues, retires the stager/events/stream, and frees `Impl::owned` (prefill.cpp:536–560). Copy Prefill stats before reset because reset clears them. Do not reset from a callback, mid-prompt, cancellation path, or while a chunk can still be in use.
- After prompt completion, verification/decode runs and may issue commit, expert-copy, and adaptive work. Before changing mapped cache pages, drain/commit the verifier and adaptive copies, then device-synchronize, matching the existing between-request VRAM command's ordering (generate.cpp:7242–7254). A GEN is eligible only after it has completed and the server is between requests.
- Before the next prompt, return the cache to its base mapped size, remove any host residency entries that name the unmapped tail, upload the corrected device residency table, then call `sp.init` again before any `sp.run`. Prompt-cache reuse, partial restore paths and short-read routing need separate analysis because they can route prompt positions through verifier windows instead of the ordinary batched path.

Same-base cache expansion requirements
1. Reserve virtual address capacity for more than 144 slots at cache open, while mapping only the initial live set. This requires new separate concepts for full reserved capacity and current mapped capacity; the current `open_segmented(want)` reserves and maps the same `want` (expert_cache.cpp:176–217, 295–377).
2. Use actual Level Zero/SYCL virtual memory only. The wrapper checks `ext_oneapi_virtual_mem` (`src/core/gpu.cpp:161–173`), reserves with `reserve_virtual_mem`, allocates physical segments with `physical_mem`, and maps them at the reserved address (181–209). If the selected device/runtime lacks the aspect or mapping fails, reject the cache-growth arm and preserve the baseline; do not substitute malloc or pretend ordinary allocations are same-base growth. No B570 runtime capability probe was performed.
3. Preserve the actual per-layer cache policy. The measured 144 slots correspond to three slots per each of 48 layers under `--expert-cache 128 --expert-cache-per-layer` (historical source/accounting in R306). Simply make `full_slots=240` and map the first 144 global slots: `layer_slot_range()` partitions by full slot count and a 240-slot layout gives five per layer (expert_cache.cpp:430–439), so a globally contiguous live prefix does not provide three mapped slots to every layer. A naive grow could make layers' old slot quotas inaccessible or admit an unmapped slot. A correct design needs a page/granularity-aware per-layer extent layout, stable `slot_off` entries for the full reserved capacity, mapped extents that preserve each layer's existing three slots, and added two-slot extents for the cache arm. A 240-slot target (+96, exactly two more per layer) is a cleaner bounded contrast than +128, but its mapped bytes depend on actual per-layer expert blob sizes and VMM page rounding.
4. At initial verifier creation, bind the full reserved slot-offset table/capacity, not just the 144 live mapped slots, while the residency table only marks mapped and filled slots. The current code binds `vh.n_slots=xcache.slots()` (5857–5859); that must be changed in concert with the new capacity API. Then stable cache base and full slot-offset addresses can let existing verifier graphs refer to later-mapped slots without graph rebuild, provided runtime kernels consult only valid `d_res` entries and do not touch unmapped slots. Verify this contract in all resident/device-plan/segmented verifier branches before claiming the graph survives growth.
5. Preserve/update every cache reader, including `Drive`/`TokenHits`, verifier `VerifyHits`, device and host residency tables, and any `TokenGraph`. The actual segmented route on B570 historically suppresses token-graph capture when concurrent host handoff is unavailable (generate.cpp:5541–5544), but the owner must confirm the qualified runtime's route; do not assume explicit segmented mode alone disables it. A stable base/offset layout is needed precisely to avoid stale captured pointers.
6. Load new slot payloads from the still-live immutable expert source/profile and wait for all copies before publishing `host_res`/`d_res`. Existing mapped cache bytes and the session must remain intact. No VRAM-to-RAM bounce of prior expert data is needed for new slots; an evicted tail slot can be re-filled from the host source when it is remapped.

Serialized GEN-only transition proposed for a future implementation
- Limit the first arm to one device, `--batch 0`, no MTP, no conversation-cache/RESTORE/SAVE, fresh GEN prompts with prompt-cache disabled, no concurrent pipeline, no borrowed cache span, unchanged prefill chunk and source/profile. It may use only one GEN at a time and must wait for all verifier/adaptive work between requests.
- After each successful batched prompt and its existing completion/refill work, copy Prefill stats, call `sp.reset()` and verify its release/drain outcome. Then map the per-layer tail in the pre-reserved cache, fill the selected additional profile experts from `srcp`, and upload the complete host/device residency state. Decode uses the already initialized verifier only if its full-capacity address/table contract was established at startup.
- At the beginning of the next fresh GEN, wait/drain, unmap the additional per-layer extents, invalidate their residency entries and upload the map; reinitialize `sp` with the same `--prefill 8192 --no-prefill-borrow` settings before reading prompt chunks. After that prompt, repeat retirement/growth. If no tail mapping leaves enough memory for Prefill init plus the existing 512-MiB/specified VRAM reserve and other fixed allocations, stop and retain the baseline.
- With no MTP, the `SAVE`/`RESTORE` command is rejected by source (generate.cpp:7903–7905), and conversation parking/save behavior is disabled at 5763–5767; nonetheless exclude those commands, prompt-cache restore/reuse, and `--batch` from the first proof. Batch mode can decode while prompts are read (7807–7816, 8904–8908), so its owner/queue set is incompatible with this serialized transition.
- Do not change the 262,144 context/session or the 32,768 resident int8 KV tier. Preserve QSA, GDN convolution/recurrent, PLE, PLE history, token positions and all KVG physical mappings; cache growth consumes only additional cache-reservation bytes after Prefill retirement. Assert their state fingerprints at prompt/decode/request boundaries.

Bounded comparison and uncertainty
After the current GEN128 qualification closes, an opt-in 144-vs-240 per-layer cache contrast on the same fresh 32K GEN128 prompt/continuation is a reasonable first performance screen. Hold the exact controller argv, source, runtime, selected chunk/ring, workers, prompt tokens, decode settings and all non-cache owners fixed. Capture actual CLI-selected route (including `--serve`, `--no-prefill-borrow`, and whether `--vram-elastic` is active), prefill allocation/free delta, VMM capability/granularity, live/full cache slots, each mapped byte range, source-filled slot identities/hashes, hit/lookups, decode latency, host free memory, and device fault/normal QUIT evidence. No exact Prefill bytes returned, VMM capability, slot-fill transfer time, hit improvement or throughput gain is established by this audit. Do not add 1.776 GiB from R321/R279 as measured available VRAM; that retained earlier no-borrow count is only an older source/configuration scale estimate.

Decision
Do not prototype by simply calling `sp.reset()` after prompt or by raising `ExpertCache::grow`'s target. In persistent serve the prompt workspace is needed again, the verifier already owns a fixed slot table/graph, the current reservation has no extra capacity, and per-layer slot ranges cannot grow as a naive global prefix. A safe candidate is a focused reserve-vs-map/per-layer-extent API plus a paired Prefill reset/reinit lifecycle and startup verifier binding to reserved capacity. Until the selected CLI/runtime confirms real VMM capability and the new owners/slot layout are validated, retain the current 144-slot service path.

- The supplied qualified controller argv confirms `--serve`; no active Main receipt was read. Task-supplied settings define the requested route; exact `--vram-elastic`, prompt-cache, batch, ring, and runtime VMM aspects remain requirements to capture before implementing this arm.
- R321 `research-no-mtp-prefill-retirement-decode-cache-growth-round321-v1.txt` is preserved; this report corrects its one-shot route seam. Prior R216 `research-pristine-xe0142-prefill-decode-transition-owner-admission-round216-v1.txt` is old pristine source evidence and not a runtime proof for candidate W.
